constitution.title: Namibian Constitution, as amended to the Third Amendment Act 8 of 2014
constitution.note: Arts. 28-29 (President: direct, more than half of the valid votes or a second ballot between the top two; five-year term; by-election on a vacancy more than a year before the term ends), 46 (96 elected members of the National Assembly and up to 8 appointed without a vote), 48 (vacancies filled from the party list), 49 and Schedule 4 (party lists by proportional representation), 50 (five-year Assembly), 51 (Speaker elected by the Assembly), 57 (dissolution), 69-70 (National Council of three members per region elected by each regional council), 94B (Electoral Commission), 102 and 105-109 (regions, constituencies, regional councils, management committees), 111 (local authorities), 132(3) (constitutional referendum), 133-134 (the 1989 Constituent Assembly as the first National Assembly; the first President elected by it), and Schedule 8 (laws repealed at independence, including the South-West Africa Constitution Act 39 of 1968, the Rehoboth Self-Government Act 56 of 1976, and the Representative Authorities Proclamation AG 8 of 1980). Read in the annotated statute text that the Legal Assistance Centre hosts from the Government Gazette.

third-amendment.title: Namibian Constitution Third Amendment Act 8 of 2014
third-amendment.note: Raised the elected National Assembly from 72 to 96 members and the appointed members from 6 to 8, the National Council from two to three members per region, and created the office of Vice-President. Read in the annotated statute text that the Legal Assistance Centre hosts from the Government Gazette.

electoral-act.title: Electoral Act 5 of 2014
electoral-act.note: Ss. 63-64 (general elections and by-elections; by-elections only for the President and regional councils), 72-88 (nominations; party lists for the National Assembly and local authorities; an unopposed candidate is declared elected), 109-113 (determination of results and their publication in the Gazette), 117-134 (referendums by presidential proclamation), and 154 (party funding). Replaced the Electoral Act 24 of 1992. Read in the annotated statute text that the Legal Assistance Centre hosts from the Government Gazette.

regional-councils-act.title: Regional Councils Act 22 of 1992, as amended
regional-councils-act.note: S. 7 (general elections at intervals not exceeding five years since Act 12 of 2010), s. 8 (five-year term), s. 10(3) (a by-election within 90 days of a vacancy), ss. 26-27 (each regional council elects its National Council members). The annotation records the first regional council elections as 30 November to 3 December 1992 (Proclamation 39 of 1992) and Proclamation 25 of 2013, which split Kavango into Kavango East and Kavango West. Read in the annotated statute text that the Legal Assistance Centre hosts from the Government Gazette.

local-authorities-act.title: Local Authorities Act 23 of 1992, as amended
local-authorities-act.note: S. 6 (municipal councils of 7-15, town councils of 7-12, and village councils of 5 members, elected on party lists), s. 8 (general elections at intervals not exceeding five years), ss. 11-12 (each council elects its mayor or chairperson), s. 13 (vacancies filled from the party list). Read in the annotated statute text that the Legal Assistance Centre hosts from the Government Gazette.

traditional-authorities-act.title: Traditional Authorities Act 25 of 2000
traditional-authorities-act.note: Chiefs and heads of traditional communities are designated under the customary law of each community and recognized by the Minister; senior traditional councillors are appointed or elected under customary law. Read in the annotated statute text that the Legal Assistance Centre hosts from the Government Gazette.

governors-act.title: Special Advisers and Regional Governors Appointment Act 6 of 1990, as amended
governors-act.note: Section 2 (regional representatives) was deleted from 30 November 1992 by the Regional Councils Act; the Amendment Act 15 of 2010 (24 November 2010) provides for regional governors appointed by the President. Read in the annotated statute text that the Legal Assistance Centre hosts from the Government Gazette.

classes.name: General election of members of the National Assembly
classes.locator: Namibian Constitution, Arts. 46(1)(a), 49, and Schedule 4 (members elected on party lists by proportional representation), 50 (five-year term), and 133 (the Constituent Assembly elected in 1989 is the first National Assembly)
classes.finest_note: One national list contest; the Commission's 2014 table gives each party's votes by constituency, and the 2024 Gazette notice gives national totals only (its post-election report gives ballots by constituency)
classes.note: Closed party lists in a single national constituency, seats by largest remainder against a quota of valid votes divided by elected seats (Schedule 4). 72 elected members from 1989 to 2009 and 96 since 2014 (Third Amendment Act 8 of 2014), plus up to 6 (now 8) members appointed by the President without a vote. The 1989 election, 7-11 November 1989, was to the Constituent Assembly under Security Council resolution 435 (1978), run by the Administrator-General under United Nations supervision; Art. 133 made it the first National Assembly. A vacancy is filled from the party's list, so there are no by-elections. Namibians abroad vote at foreign missions.

classes.name: Election of the President
classes.locator: Namibian Constitution, Art. 28(2) (direct, universal and equal suffrage; more than 50 per cent of the valid votes, else a second ballot between the two leading candidates) and Art. 29 (five-year term, two terms, by-election on a vacancy more than a year before the term ends)
classes.finest_note: The 2024 Gazette notice gives national totals by candidate; constituency counts are announced but not yet found in a published file
classes.note: Held with the National Assembly election. The first President was elected by the Constituent Assembly on 16 February 1990 (Art. 134; see president_constituent_assembly), so the first popular vote was in 1994. No second ballot has been needed. The Commission's turnout table lists 1989 under presidential elections, but the 1989 ballot was for the Constituent Assembly only. A presidential by-election under Art. 29(4)(b) has never been held.

cadence.runoff_rule: Art. 28(2)(b): more than 50 per cent of the valid votes, else a second ballot between the two candidates with the most votes

cadence.vacancy_rule: Art. 29(4): a by-election if the vacancy occurs more than one year before the next presidential election, else succession under Art. 34

classes.name: Referendum
classes.locator: Electoral Act 5 of 2014, s. 119 (the President may proclaim a referendum on a constitutional bill under Art. 132(3), on any bill or other matter, and must proclaim one the National Assembly resolves on under Art. 63(2)(g)) and ss. 117-134
classes.note: Provided for since independence but never held: no referendum proclamation has been issued and the Commission's results pages list none.

classes.name: Election of members of the National Council
classes.name_en: National Council, elected by the regional councils
classes.locator: Namibian Constitution, Art. 69(1) (three members from each region elected by its regional council from amongst their members) and Art. 70 (five-year term); Regional Councils Act 22 of 1992, ss. 26-27
classes.disposition_reason: Each regional council elects its members at a council sitting from amongst its own councillors; there is no public ballot, and the Commission publishes no count.
classes.note: Two members per region (26) until 2015 and three (42) since, under the Third Amendment Act 8 of 2014.

classes.name: Election of the Speaker
classes.name_en: Speaker of the National Assembly and Chairperson of the National Council
classes.locator: Namibian Constitution, Art. 51(1) (the National Assembly elects a member as Speaker at its first sitting) and Art. 73 (the National Council elects its Chairperson)
classes.disposition_reason: An internal vote of each house at its first sitting, recorded in its debates rather than run or published as an election.

classes.name: Election of the first President by the Constituent Assembly
classes.name_en: First President, elected by the Constituent Assembly
classes.locator: Namibian Constitution, Art. 134(1): the first President of Namibia shall be the person elected to that office by the Constituent Assembly by a simple majority of all its members
classes.disposition_reason: A vote of the 72 members of the Constituent Assembly, recorded in its debates; there was no public ballot.

classes.name: General election of members of regional councils
classes.name_en: Regional councils, one councillor per constituency
classes.locator: Namibian Constitution, Art. 106 (each constituency elects one member of the regional council; the candidate with the most votes is elected; all on the same day, fixed by presidential proclamation)
classes.finest_note: Constituency; the Commission's tables and Gazette notices give each candidate's votes by constituency
classes.note: Single-member constituencies by plurality. 95 constituencies in 1992, 102 in 1998, 107 in 2004 and 2010, and 121 since the 2013 delimitation, which also split Kavango into two regions (14 regions). A candidate nominated unopposed is declared elected without a poll (26 of 121 in 2015). Terms ran six years until the Regional Councils Amendment Act 12 of 2010 and five since; from 2010 the elections fall on the same days as the local authority elections. Polls in a few places in 2020 were rerun on 26 February 2021.

classes.name_en: Mayors and council chairpersons, elected by the councils
classes.locator: Local Authorities Act 23 of 1992, ss. 11-12 (each council elects its mayor and deputy mayor, or chairperson and vice-chairperson, from its members)
classes.disposition_reason: Each council elects its office-bearers from among its members at its first meeting; the state does not run or publish these votes.

classes.name: Management committees, chairpersons, and governors of regions
classes.locator: Namibian Constitution, Art. 109 (each regional council elects its management committee and chairperson); Special Advisers and Regional Governors Appointment Act 6 of 1990 as amended by Act 15 of 2010 (governors appointed by the President)
classes.disposition_reason: Chairpersons and management committees are elected by each regional council from among its members, and since 2010 regional governors are appointed by the President; neither is a public ballot.

classes.name: Designation of chiefs and traditional councillors
classes.locator: Traditional Authorities Act 25 of 2000, ss. 4-6 (designation of chiefs or heads under the customary law of each community, recognized by the Minister)
classes.disposition_reason: Chiefs and traditional councillors are designated under each community's customary law, not at a poll the Electoral Commission runs, and no results are published.

classes.name: Selection of party candidates and lists
classes.locator: Electoral Act 5 of 2014, ss. 77 and 86 (parties submit their lists) and s. 80 (regional council candidates are nominated by parties or registered voters)
classes.disposition_reason: Parties choose their candidates and rank their lists under their own constitutions; the state neither runs nor publishes these contests.

classes.name: Appointment of judges
classes.locator: Namibian Constitution, Art. 82 (judges appointed by the President on the recommendation of the Judicial Service Commission)

classes.name: Legislative Assembly for the Territory of South-West Africa
classes.name_en: South West Africa Legislative Assembly (white electorate)
classes.locator: Namibian Constitution, Schedule 8 (laws repealed at independence: the South-West Africa Constitution Act 39 of 1968, the Rehoboth Self-Government Act 56 of 1976, and the Representative Authorities Proclamation AG 8 of 1980 with the proclamations for each authority)
classes.disposition_reason: Elected by white voters only under South African administration; the results were printed in the Official Gazette of South West Africa, of which no official copy is online, and the Commission's records begin in 1989.
classes.note: Constituted under the South-West Africa Constitution Act 42 of 1925 and later Act 39 of 1968, both under South Africa; replaced by the Legislative Assembly of the Representative Authority of the Whites in 1980. The bounds are year boundaries. A referendum of white voters in May 1977 on the Turnhalle proposals also falls under this administration and is not yet cited from an official record.

classes.name: Election of the Constituent Assembly of South West Africa, 1978
classes.locator: Security Council resolution 439 (1978), declaring the elections held in the territory in December 1978 null and void
classes.disposition_reason: Held by the South African administration without United Nations supervision and declared null and void by the Security Council; the results were printed in the Official Gazette of South West Africa, of which no official copy is online.
classes.note: Polling 4-8 December 1978. The assembly became a National Assembly with legislative powers in 1979 and was dissolved in January 1983.

classes.name: Legislative assemblies of the representative authorities
classes.locator: Namibian Constitution, Schedule 8 (laws repealed at independence: the South-West Africa Constitution Act 39 of 1968, the Rehoboth Self-Government Act 56 of 1976, and the Representative Authorities Proclamation AG 8 of 1980 with the proclamations for each authority)
classes.disposition_reason: Second-tier legislative assemblies elected on separate ethnic rolls under South African administration and abolished at independence; their results were printed in the Official Gazette of South West Africa, of which no official copy is online.
classes.note: Representative authorities of the Whites, Coloureds, Ovambos, Kavangos, Caprivians, Damaras, Namas, Tswanas, and Hereros under Proclamation AG 8 of 1980 and the proclamations for each. The bounds are year boundaries.

classes.name: Kaptein and Council of Rehoboth
classes.locator: Namibian Constitution, Schedule 8 (laws repealed at independence: the South-West Africa Constitution Act 39 of 1968, the Rehoboth Self-Government Act 56 of 1976, and the Representative Authorities Proclamation AG 8 of 1980 with the proclamations for each authority)
classes.disposition_reason: Elected by the Rehoboth Baster community under the Rehoboth Self-Government Act 56 of 1976, repealed at independence; no official record of the results is online.
